object: German-born theoretical physicist (1879–1955). Nobel Prize 1921 for the photoelectric effect. Architect of special and general relativity who helped launch quantum theory, then spent Solvay trying to prove it incomplete. The problems he raised — locality, realism, the EPR paradox — still haunt physics a century later.
